requirements.text: open a new hire onboarding case with a description explaining the equipment delay. Assign the case to Robin Monroe and ensure the IT Support L1 team is working on it
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 11 AND opened_for = 9 AND account_number = 'ACC-412-234' AND assigned_to = 31 AND assignment_group = 1 AND status = 'awaiting_acceptance' AND request_status = 'requested' AND priority = 'moderate' AND coe_type = 'Talent Management' AND short_description LIKE 'Service: %, Subject: %, Detail: %'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id in the seed is 60)
new hire onboarding is hr_service 11 'New Hire Onboarding' (active)
Steven Hernandez is user 9 with hr_profile 9; opened_for references hr_profile
ACC-412-234, given beside Steven Hernandez's name, is taken as the case's account_number
Robin Monroe is user 31 (active); IT Support L1 is group 1
assigned_to = 31 is stated by the request and added to the benchmark check's cells
policy: assigning a case to a user or group sets status awaiting_acceptance and request_status requested
priority not stated; the policy's default is moderate
coe_type Talent Management kept from the benchmark check; service 11's topic detail 24 sits in topic category 10 (Talent Acquisition), whose coe_type is Talent Management
short_description follows the policy's case format 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: .', as the benchmark check tests

requirements.text: Assign the case to Robin Monroe and ensure the IT Support L1 team is working on it
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 44 AND group_id = 1 AND user_id = 31
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id in the seed is 43)
Robin Monroe (user 31) is a member of group 9 only in the seed, not of IT Support L1 (group 1)
policy: a case must be assigned to an active user in its assignment group, and an assignee outside the group is added to it
implied by the request, not stated

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement, value and disposition; no disagreements. The case requirement adds assigned_to = 31 (Robin Monroe), which the request states and the benchmark check leaves out. hr_case has no description column apart from short_description, whose wording is free text, so only the policy format the benchmark tests is required, not words about the laptop and badge delay; the policy's 30-120 character limit on short_description is a format rule the benchmark does not test and is left out. opened_by is not tested: the requester could be read as Steven Hernandez, who reported the delay, or as the acting user Karen Watkins, and neither the request nor the policy settles which. source and account_type are not stated and have no policy default, so they are not tested. The acting user is an admin, whom the policy bars from routine HR case work while granting full write access; the request is explicit and both benchmark checks expect the case and membership to be written, so the request is treated as permitted.
